# ADR conventions

How this repo keeps its decision log, shared by every code-kestrel repo. The index is [`README.md`](README.md); a new record starts from [`template.md`](template.md).

## Using the log

1. **Before planning, list the log:** `grep -H -m2 -E '^# |Status:' docs/adr/[0-9]*.md` prints each record's title and status. Read any record the work touches. Cite the ADRs you rely on in the plan, the PR body and any critic brief. Do not re-derive a decision that has a record.
2. **A critic finding against an accepted record** is filed as `CHALLENGES ADR <id>: <what changed>`, not as a defect. A diff that makes a significant decision (list below) without a record is a finding.
3. **Re-open when the world moved.** "It did not work" is a fact about a date, a tool version and a device. When a record's *Revisit when* condition is met, say so and propose a superseding record. A product, look or product-affecting data-model decision is the user's, via dialog. A purely technical decision may be superseded act-then-show by a session pre-authorized for that work; the new record says so in *Deciders*.
4. **Record significant decisions in the same PR** that makes them, never as a follow-up.
5. **Keep the log current in the same PR.** When code, CLAUDE.md or a README stops matching an accepted record, correct the stale doc, or supersede the record and flip the old record's Status in the same commit.

## When a record is owed

A user dialog pick on architecture, product model or look; a new or retired hard constraint; a reversal; a platform floor or ceiling; a vendor, dependency or hosting choice; a process rule with an incident behind it that shapes code; an option a critic argued against that was kept. **Not owed:** bug fixes, reversible implementation detail, anything a single PR can undo without anyone noticing.

## Shape

- **Files:** `docs/adr/YYYY-MM-DD-short-imperative-title.md`: the decision date, then a kebab-case title that names the decision (`2026-09-24-sign-in-with-apple-only.md`, not `2026-09-24-auth.md`). Dated ids let two open PRs avoid colliding on a counter. Records named `NNNN-` before 2026-09-24 keep their names; `0000` seeds a new log. A record's **id** is its filename without `.md`. Copy `template.md`. One decision per record; two decisions in one dialog are two records.
- **No index table.** The folder is the log. `README.md` is the front page plus any labelled repo-specific additions.
- **Sections:** header lines *Status*, *Date*, *Deciders*, *Decided in*, *Implemented* (a merge sha or PR, else `no`; a missing line is a warning, never a failure), *Supersedes* or *Amends*; then *Context and problem*, *Decision* ("We will..."), *Options considered* (the losers and why, above all the one a critic argued for), *Consequences*, *Confirmation* (the behaviour, check, grep or critic line that proves it, never just a test file name, or "none, judgement"), *Revisit when* (the conditions, or "nothing foreseen"; never omitted).
- **Statuses:** `proposed`, `accepted`, `rejected`, `deprecated`, `superseded by <id>`. The user's dialog pick, or the merge of the PR that carries it, makes a proposal `accepted`.
- **Immutable once accepted**, except the Status line, supersession or amendment links, and fact corrections. Changing course is a new record with *Supersedes <id>*; the old Status flips. Overriding one clause of a record that otherwise stands is a new record with *Amends <id>*; the old Status becomes `accepted; amended by <id>`. A fact that was wrong when written is corrected in place when nothing is re-decided, with a header line `Amended YYYY-MM-DD: <what and why>`. Nothing is deleted.
- **Length:** one screen. Design detail stays in the plan doc; the record links it. Dates are the decision's day; a backfilled record says "backfilled YYYY-MM-DD".

## One home per fact

| Question | Its one home |
|---|---|
| Why is it this way, what lost, when does it stop holding? | `docs/adr/` (the PR description links the record and stops) |
| What shipped, and its how-to traps? | `git log --first-parent main` (each squash commit carries its PR description; `CHANGELOG.md` is the frozen record before 2026-09-24) |
| What happened: the incident behind a rule? | the repo's incident log (`docs/HISTORY.md` or equivalent), if any |
| How to behave now? | `CLAUDE.md` (a hard constraint cites its ADR for the why) |
| What next, and the board's state? | the [Fletchwork Backlog](https://github.com/orgs/Fletchwork/projects/1) board (issues); `docs/ROADMAP.md` keeps direction, `HANDOFF.md` keeps traps |
| How we build it: design detail? | the plan doc (its decisions become ADRs) |
| What the project is and how to set it up? | `README.md` |
| Kestrel's private working notes? | auto-memory, never a source of truth; a decision found only there gets a record |

Everything else links, never restates. **When two disagree:** the ADR wins on the why and the options; git on what shipped; CLAUDE.md on what to do today; the code on what runs. Fix the disagreement in one PR and say which side was stale. On the ADR side only a Status flip, a supersession link or a new record; an accepted body is never rewritten.
